scope: Theorem 1.1 of the manuscript “A linear cycle-and-edge decomposition of every graph” (preprints/A-linear-cycle-and-edge-decomposition-of-every-graph-September-24-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 181 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4aa44187578ea59b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 1. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There is an absolute constant C > 0 such that, for every finite simple undirected graph G with n vertices, E(G) has a partition into at most Cn parts, each of which is the edge set of a cycle or consists of a single edge.
